> explicitly marked **Status: Gap**, which denotes an obligation derived from the

>
> **Applicability note on responsive design.** CodeGenerator ships no web UI. Its only

> libraries. The responsive-design obligations that would apply to a web application are

> versus plain consoles).

## L1-001: Model-Driven Artifact Generation
The system must generate files, projects, and solutions from lightweight object models
supplied by a caller, dispatching each model to the generation strategies registered for
its type without the caller naming a strategy.

## L1-002: Language-Agnostic Syntax Generation
The system must render source-code text from syntax models for every supported target
language, selecting the generating strategy from the model's runtime type.

## L1-003: Fluent Model Builders
The system must provide fluent builders that let a caller construct valid generation
models in a minimal number of statements, so that agents and applications can describe an
artifact far more compactly than the generated output.

## L1-004: Template Processing Engine
The system must render text templates against a token dictionary, expose code-generation
helper filters to template authors, and allow a template to abort its own output.

## L1-005: Template Discovery, Styles, and Conventions
The system must discover template sets from disk and from embedded assembly resources,
organize them into a language-and-style matrix, and derive output paths from template
paths by convention rather than configuration.

## L1-006: Multi-Language and Multi-Framework Generation Coverage
The system must generate idiomatic code for .NET, Python, Flask, Angular, React, React
Native, Playwright, and Detox, and must expose each target as a separately consumable
package with its own service-registration entry point.

## L1-007: .NET Solution and Architecture Scaffolding
The system must scaffold complete .NET solutions — solution files, projects, project
references, and layered architectures — including clean-architecture, CQRS, and
domain-driven-design structures and full-stack applications.

## L1-008: Schema Ingestion and Normalization
The system must accept external interface and model definitions in multiple schema
formats, detect the format automatically, and normalize them into a single internal model
that the generators consume.

## L1-009: Declarative YAML Scaffolding
The system must scaffold an entire multi-project workspace from a single declarative YAML
configuration file, validating that configuration before any file is written.

## L1-010: Command Line Interface
The system must expose its generation capabilities through a command line tool that can
create a new code-generator project, scaffold from configuration, and install supporting
assets into a consuming repository.

## L1-011: Hierarchical Configuration
The system must resolve every configuration setting from an ordered set of sources so that
a more specific source always overrides a more general one.

## L1-012: Input and Model Validation
The system must validate all caller-supplied input — CLI options, configuration files, and
generation models — before performing work, and must report every validation failure with
the offending property identified.

## L1-013: Error Handling and Exit Codes
The system must classify every failure into a stable category, surface a stable machine-
readable error code, and terminate the CLI with an exit code that identifies the failure
class.

## L1-014: Transactional Generation and Rollback
The system must treat a generation run as a unit of work: on failure it must undo the
filesystem changes it made, and on success it must discard its undo state.

## L1-015: Dry Run and Preview
The system must be able to report exactly what a generation run would create without
writing any file or executing any external command.

## L1-016: Interactive and Non-Interactive Operation
The system must adapt to its execution environment, prompting for missing input when
attached to an interactive terminal and running unattended when it is not.

## L1-017: Console Output and Progress Reporting
The system must communicate progress, results, and failures through structured console
output that degrades gracefully when rich terminal rendering is unavailable.

## L1-018: Incremental Generation into Existing Projects
The system must add generated artifacts to an existing project, detecting the project's
type from its contents and resolving collisions with existing files under an explicit
policy.

## L1-019: Extensibility and Plugin Architecture
The system must discover and register generation strategies from arbitrary assemblies
without code changes to the core, and must isolate a faulty plugin from the rest of a run.

## L1-020: Post-Generation Verification
The system must be able to verify that generated output is well formed by running
verification steps against it and reporting the outcome of each step.

## L1-021: Dependency and Package Version Management
The system must resolve third-party package versions for generated projects from a
centrally managed manifest so that generated output does not carry versions hard-coded at
scattered call sites.

## L1-022: Resilience, Cancellation, and Process Execution
The system must survive transient filesystem contention, honour user cancellation
promptly, and execute external toolchain commands consistently across operating systems.

## L1-023: Security and Safe Generation
The system must refuse to write outside its designated output tree, must not execute or
load untrusted input implicitly, and must not disclose secrets through its output.

## L1-024: Performance and Resource Efficiency
The system must keep per-model generation overhead low by caching reflection, templates,
and manifests, so that generating many artifacts in one run does not degrade
proportionally to reflection cost.

## L1-025: Observability and Diagnostics
The system must correlate all activity within a single invocation, and must be able to
report its execution environment and per-step timings on demand.

## L1-026: Packaging, Distribution, and Release Automation
The system must ship as versioned NuGet packages and as an installable .NET global tool,
and must publish new versions automatically when component sources change.

## L1-027: Test Coverage and Quality Gates
The system must maintain automated unit and integration test coverage for every component,
and must block release of a change that fails to build or test.
